  Due 11.59pm Friday, Week 1
</Callout>

### Download your map

On the David Rumsey website, there is an option to download your map. Return to your map, and locate this option. Choose a medium size download and either JPG or PNG.

Make sure you note down what dimensions you downloaded.

## Getting Used to Adobe Illustrator

<Callout kind="alert" collapsed="false">
  You need to have signed up to **Adobe Creative Suite** to take this studio.&#x20;

  See "Getting Started" for more information.
</Callout>

### Open Adobe Illustrator for Web

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open your web browser" title-type="p">
    The best performance is with Chrome or Microsoft Edge.&#x20;
  </Step>

  <Step title="Access the App" title-type="p">
    Go to <a href="https://illustrator.adobe.com/?trackingid=G4FRYP8K&mv=in-product&mv2=cc" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><u>Illustrator on the web (Beta) </u></a>to access the app on your browser.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign In" title-type="p">
    Select **Sign in** and access your Illustrator files using your credentials.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Callout kind="info" collapsed="false">
  Adobe Illustrator for Web is still in Beta - which means it's still be tested. This means it can be a bit buggy, so make sure you save your work at regular intervals!
</Callout>

### Open a new document

<Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776808381608-w3hh80dqbfl-Screenshot-of-the-Illustrator-on-web--Beta--homepa-1.avif?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="720" height="465" alt="" />

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create Your Document" title-type="p">
    On the <a href="https://illustrator.adobe.com/?trackingid=G4FRYP8K&mv=in-product&mv2=cc" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><u>home page</u></a>, select **Create**
  </Step>

  <Step title="Set Your Dimensions" title-type="p">
    In the dialog that appears you can set your dimensions. Any dimensions are fine for now.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Explore the Sidebar" title-type="p">
    On the sidebar, there are a range of different tools. Play around with them to see what they do. If you make a mistake, you can just make a new document.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Annotate Your Map

Okay, now we need to get serious about annotating your map. Your final assessment for this module requires you to annotate a map, and design a PDF document with a short critique of your map.

<Card title="Cartographic Interpretation" href="/cartographic-interpretation" horizontal="false" target="_self">
  Card description...
</Card>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create Your Document" title-type="p">
    Create a new document, and use the dimensions of your map that you downloaded from Rumsey. &#x20;

    <Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776808848836-pgoraio93b-pasted-image-1776808847016.png?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="1200" height="775" alt="" />
  </Step>

  <Step title="Place your Map" title-type="p">
    Using the Place tool, select your map and place on the artboard.&#x20;

    <Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776812624228-hl0x7gjwucb-pasted-image-1776812622112.png?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="2058" height="1242" alt="" />
  </Step>

  <Step title="Resize your Map" title-type="p">
    Drag the edges of the you have just placed in or out in order to fill the page. You can also use the **Artboard Tool&#x20;**&#x74;o resize the artboard so you have space on the side of the map for your essay.

    <Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776812821472-0kav8lwt5a3-pasted-image-1776812819178.png?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="2058" height="1242" alt="" />
  </Step>

  <Step title="Lock your map" title-type="p">
    Lock your map in place using the Lock tool. This prevents it from moving about or being selected as you do your annotation. If you need to unlock it, just click the lock again.

    <Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776814934942-u8mmerxofan-pasted-image-1776814932807.png?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="2058" height="1242" alt="" />
  </Step>

  <Step title="Use Your Skills!" title-type="p">
    Use your new Illustrator skills to annotate your map, and write out your critique. Feel free to change the size of the artboard, or the map depending on how it pans out.&#x20;

    <Image src="https://blob-cdn.documentation.ai/org-6332b605-3e6a-4ce1-a00b-8a907a798c06/doc-12cb6eab-9bd9-48e3-96d6-1b96ec509835/1776815565541-5y1kd5h1rjp-pasted-image-1776815563681.png?fm=auto&auto=compress%2Cformat" width="2770" height="1392" alt="" />
  </Step>

  <Step title="DO NOT FORGET TO SAVE" title-type="p">
    Do not forget to save your map at regular intervals to the Adobe Creative Cloud.&#x20;
  </Step>

  <Step title="Export and Submit" title-type="p">
    When you are ready, export your map as a PDF and submit to the Cartographic Interpretation Assessment.&#x20;
  </Step>
</Steps>
